title: Understanding the Problem
text: To find the mean squared error (MSE), we need to understand the relationship between the input colors and the output predictions. The task is to predict whether someone is a night owl (0) or an early bird (1) based on their favorite color.

title: Optimal Value of Theta
text: The optimal value of theta minimizes the mean squared error between the predicted values and the actual values. In this case, theta represents the parameter that best fits the data.

title: Calculating Mean Squared Error
text: The mean squared error is calculated as the average of the squares of the differences between the predicted values and the actual values. Use the formula: $$MSE=\frac{\sum \left(y_{pred}-y_{actual}\right)^2}{n}$$, where $$n$$ is the number of data points.

title: Compute the Predictions
text: Assume the optimal theta gives predictions that perfectly match the actual values. What would the predictions be for the given data points?

title: Calculate the Squared Differences
text: Calculate the squared differences between the predicted values and the actual values for each data point.

title: Compute the Mean Squared Error
text: Using the squared differences, compute the mean squared error by averaging them.
